recipe.notes:
What the model is. A multimodal late-interaction (multi-vector) retriever: one
L2-normalized 128-dim vector per kept token, retrieval score = fp32 MaxSim,
client-side. The checkpoint is a native sentence-transformers export -- no
custom Python code anywhere (the card says so; the repo has no auto_map, no
modeling file, and the modules.json lists only native ST classes). The
pipeline: the Qwen3.5 backbone (bidirectional; text_config.is_causal false)
-> 1_Dense Linear(1024 -> 128, no bias) -> 2_MultiVectorMask (documents drop
the 32 ASCII punctuation token positions; queries keep everything) ->
3_Normalize (L2). Text prompts are NOT chat-formatted on the wire: the
sentence-transformers prompts are "[Q] " and "[D] "
(config_sentence_transformers.json), both ADDED special tokens of this
tokenizer (ids 248077/248078), and the render "[Q] " + text /
"[D] " + text tokenizes to [248077|248078] + body under the engine-side
parse -- measured, and identical to the reference's (sentence-transformers
uses no split_special_tokens anywhere, unlike pplx-embed-v2-context-9b's
remote code; that divergence is why that recipe rides token_ids and this one
rides text).

The served vs reference rendering contract (stage 1):
- query shape: "[Q] " + query; every query token keeps its vector (the
  skiplist applies to documents only, skiplist_tasks ["document"]).
- document shape: "[D] " + document; every token NOT in the 32 punctuation
  ids keeps its vector. The prefix token (248078) is an added special token,
  not punctuation, so it keeps its vector on both sides -- unlike topk, where
  the prompt's own colon was dropped. The mask is the checkpoint's own
  MultiVectorMask; the recipe DECLARES it (client.document_skip_token_ids,
  resolved from skiplist_words with this tokenizer exactly as
  sentence-transformers' resolve_with_tokenizer does) and the SERVED PLUGIN
  drops the vectors at the ids it sees (client.document_skip_engine_side;
  the client counts the declared kept vectors and checks the reply).
- No content normalisation: sentence-transformers prepends the prompt
  verbatim (prepend_prompt_to_texts), so the declared normalize is [] and
  every text ships as-is. The empty-document corner that forced topk's
  omit_zero does not exist here: the reference's empty document renders the
  bare "[D] " prompt -- exactly one kept token (the prefix id, no skiplist
  word) -- and empty_doc: send renders the same frame around empty content.
  The empty-document rows gate exactly, and the wave's pairs may sample them.

Why chat_template is null: the checkpoint SHIPS chat_template.jinja at the
pinned revision and vLLM resolves it through AutoProcessor for the
pooling-chat (media) path; a missing template there is a loud per-request
error, never a silent fallback. The template is a pass-through render (system
text first, then vision markers, then text parts; no im-start/im-end
wrappers), which is why the reference's chat-templated TEXT renders are
byte-identical to the plain prompts the /pooling route reads (the route
applies no template -- poolings/protocol.py at the tag). Shipping a copy
would add a second source of truth for a file the engine already pins through
the revision. The harness's stage-1 template check cannot render a
messages-based template (it renders query/document variables), so the
recipe's test pins the image wrapper structure directly instead.

The declared fields that make the card's behaviour expressible with the
product:
- The document-side skiplist -> client.document_skip_token_ids (the 32 ids
  above), applied ENGINE-SIDE (client.document_skip_engine_side: true):
  vLLM v0.31.0's pooling route cannot return the engine's per-position
  token ids, so the pplx-late plugin's pooler drops the rule's positions
  from the token ids it sees -- the render's own ids, a media document's
  head and vision markers included -- and the wire carries only kept
  vectors. The rule is DOCUMENT-side (the checkpoint's mask declares
  skiplist_tasks: ["document"]), so the engine half also declares the
  document role gate (serve.hf_overrides.document_skip_prefix_token_id,
  the `[D] ` added token 248078): a row that does not open with it is a
  query prompt and keeps every position, which is what the reference's
  encode_query does. The client cannot recompute the kept set from the
  reply: it counts the declared kept vectors instead (the sent render's ids
  outside the rule; for a media document the sent head plus the prepared
  media block) and refuses a reply whose count disagrees (a typed
  ProviderError, never a silent misalignment). The engine half of the
  declaration is serve.hf_overrides.document_skip_token_ids (the same 32
  ids; the loader refuses a mismatch, either half alone, or a rule without
  the gate). NOTE the divergence from topk's image side: this checkpoint's
  keep_only_token_ids is null, so its own mask keeps image-patch AND
  text-prefix tokens alike (everything but punctuation) -- the engine-side
  rule drops exactly those positions and nothing else, which is what the
  reference's MultiVectorMask keeps. The rule names no structural id, so a
  media render's head and vision markers are kept: the render opens with the
  `[D] ` head (client.media_head_as_system: true, the card's own system
  prompt), so the engine-side rule's document gate applies to it too and the
  client's declared count is the sent head plus the media block.
- Per-role caps -> client.query_max_tokens 1024 beside client.max_tokens
  4096: sentence_bert_config.json's per-task lengths; both caps count the
  whole rendered prompt as the engine sees it, and the fit cuts each shape's
  content span at its declared budget with the fixed head reserved
  (census-recorded).
- Per-role input -> client.media_sides: ["document"]: the card's usage
  encodes queries as text; the client refuses media on the query side (a
  typed refusal naming the field, before the media is fetched).
- The image budget -> client.image_policy {min_px 3136, max_px 1800964,
  engine_pixel_pinning: true} beside serve.mm_processor_kwargs
  {images_kwargs: {min_pixels 3136, max_pixels 1800964}} (the ONE pixel-pin
  shape of the media recipes, decided from the v0.31.0 tag source): the
  SHIPPED processor's own numbers (processor_config.json; in transformers'
  Qwen2VLImageProcessor init the min_pixels/max_pixels kwargs override the
  size dict's edges, so those are the effective bounds), pinned on both
  halves at the pinned revision -- the pin is what admits the shipped 3136 px
  floor below the family's stock 65536 (the qwen3-vl-embedding-2b shape).
  The reference (the card's path) reads the same shipped defaults. max image
  tokens: 1,800,964 / 1,024 px per merged patch, floored = 1,758.
- The projector width -> serve.hf_overrides {embed_dim: 128}: declared, not
  defaulted (the in-tree ColQwen3_5Model falls back to 128 when the config
  names no field); the plugin's load_weights cross-checks the head tensor's
  [128, 1024] shape against the module and fails loudly on any mismatch.

The folded model plugin (shared with pplx-embed-v2-context-9b): the
new PplxLateMultiVectorModel subclasses the native ColQwen3_5Model and (a)
registers the checkpoints' architecture name "Qwen3_5Model" with vLLM's
registry, (b) inherits the stock mapper that maps the checkpoints' top-level
"language_model.*" onto the class's "language_model.model.*" (visual.*
matches as-is), (c) replaces the generation-only head: neither checkpoint
ships lm_head tensors (the 0.6b ties it, the 9b declares tie_word_embeddings
false and ships none), so __init__ swaps the ParallelLMHead and
LogitsProcessor for vLLM's StageMissingLayer exactly as the
converted-pooling wrapper does -- no head parameter to load, no unused generation-head
allocation (the 9b's untied head would be 248320 x 4096 x 2 B ~ 2.0 GB at the served
bf16, the 0.6b's ~ 0.5 GB), and (d) loads the Dense head itself: each checkpoint ships it as
1_Dense/model.safetensors (one tensor, linear.weight -- [128, 1024] at 0.6b,
[128, 4096] at 9b, fp32), which the stock weight discovery never reads (the
loader's glob is non-recursive). The plugin fetches that file from the same
Hub snapshot the engine already downloaded (or the local directory when
serving from one), shape-checks the tensor against the projector the
resolved embed_dim built, renames it onto custom_text_proj.weight, and marks
the zero-initialised bias loaded (the checkpoints ship no bias; a future
revision that ships 1_Dense bias loads over the zeros). No config class is
registered for this model: model_type qwen3_5 is native to the engine's
transformers line and vLLM's own config registry parses it (trust_remote_code
stays false, nothing remote exists to execute).

Budget: max_tokens 4096 is the document cap and query_max_tokens 1024 the
query cap -- each the shape's whole rendered prompt as the engine sees it, in
the tokenizer's tokens, right truncation (sentence-transformers passes
truncation="longest_first" with the per-task max_length on every text
encode). on_overflow: cut: the content span only, the fixed head reserved,
the template re-attached (the product's fit, one budget per shape). The
card's own cut (that truncation) right-cuts the rendered prompt's ids;
reference.py renders exactly that cut, located by character offsets. Both
cuts keep the fixed head and the same text on every input measured (English,
punctuation-heavy, CJK, emoji and repeated-letter content), but the card cuts
ids, not text: when its last kept id lands inside a character spanning
several byte-level tokens (an emoji), the card's model reads that character's
leading bytes, which no text carries -- one more id than the client sends.
Hence over_cap_cut_differs (the anchor kept, the kept content differing by
that id; a stage-2 difference, the render texts are equal). max_model_len
4352 reserves the 4096-token document budget + 256 headroom; image documents
cost at most 1 + 2 + 1,758 = 1,761 tokens (the "[D] " prompt token, the
vision start/end markers, the shipped pixel budget) -- under the text cap,
so one max_model_len covers both shapes.

dtype: vLLM v0.31.0 cannot run this model in float32: the GDN prefill kernels
refuse it on every backend (the Triton/FLA path asserts "ChunkGatedDeltaRuleFunction
does not support float32. Please use bfloat16.", third_party/flash_linear_attention/
ops/chunk.py:213-215 at the tag; the flashinfer path raises the same refusal
at kernel warmup). The recipe therefore serves dtype: bfloat16 (~1.2 GB of
weights at 0.6b, ~16.8 GB at 9b; the fp32 checkpoints are cast at load)
while the REFERENCE runs each checkpoint's own fp32 (the card's
MultiVectorEncoder passes no dtype override, so the config's float32 loads) -- the
served-vs-reference difference is the cast plus the kernels, and stage 2's
tolerance gate and the wave's retrieval numbers quantify it. The int8-style
fp32 head question of the contextual sibling does not arise here: the Dense
head is a plain linear layer and runs in the pooling runner's default fp32
head dtype on the engine (vllm/config/model.py:2447-2468) -- the same
arithmetic as the reference's fp32 head up to the backbone cast.

The compile risk (flagged, shared with pplx-embed-v2-context-9b-preview):
this model's forward runs vLLM's decorated Qwen3_5Model text stack
(@support_torch_compile, qwen3_5.py:209 at the tag) -- the same machinery the
context-9b recipe's engine currently crashes in at startup on GPU (CUDA
illegal memory access inside torch.compile, under investigation). Nothing in
this recipe's serve block can avoid the stack short of --enforce-eager, which
no shipped recipe declares today and which the owner has not decided for the
family. The wave should serve this recipe WITHOUT --enforce-eager first; if
the context-9b crash reproduces here, --enforce-eager is the declared
fallback (one extra_args entry) and the finding feeds the family-level
investigation either way.

Media (the image path, both halves): serve.mm_processor_kwargs pins the
shipped numbers (nested images_kwargs, min 3136 / max 1,800,964 px -- the one
pixel-pin shape of the media recipes) and client.image_policy declares the
same numbers with engine_pixel_pinning: true (processor qwen3_vl, max_images
1, media_sides documents-only), so the client resizes and counts images
exactly as the processor would within the shipped budget. The wave's T0 probe
(one image, usage.prompt_tokens) measures the served count against
2 + ceil(H*W/1024) -- the merged patches plus the two vision markers (the
"[D] " head is the document's text, sent as a system message). The image
document rides the declared skip rule
ENGINE-SIDE: the plugin's pooler drops the rule's positions from the
render's own token ids (the rule names punctuation only, so the render's
vision markers -- and its `[D] ` head, when the client sends one -- stay)
and the client checks the reply's declared kept count (a mixed text+media
batch is still refused before sending, the text side needing its
id-aligned render). The media render opens with the trained `[D] ` head
(client.media_head_as_system: true -- the card's sentence-transformers path
sends the prompt as a system message), so it matches the reference's image
render and the engine-side rule's document gate applies to it; the wave's
probe-image check still proves the engine loaded the checkpoint's chat
template and serves image documents, and the media stage verifies their
geometry and tokens.

Reference: sentence-transformers (>= 6.0, the card's floor) MultiVectorEncoder
-- the model card's own published path, with NO custom code (the checkpoint
ships none). Its environment is the checkpoint's own requirements.txt,
declared in requirements-reference.txt (sentence-transformers and
transformers are what the reference venv installs over the image's torch;
the render mode needs only huggingface_hub and tokenizers). The reference's
load() asserts the MultiVectorEncoder surface it relies on, so a
sentence-transformers change fails loudly.

What the GPU wave must check (NOT MEASURED on CPU):
- Per-token cosine + MaxSim of served vs reference on real weights (the
  bidirectional full-attention layers must run ENCODER_ONLY; the fp32
  backbone cast to bf16 is the declared deviation the gates quantify). A
  causal/non-causal mix shows as a shift far above the vector gate.
- Stage 2's per-token counts against the reference's MultiVectorMask output;
  the engine-side rule drops exactly the reference's excluded positions, so
  the TEXT side agrees by construction -- confirm on real vectors.
- /tokenize equality on prompts over 1024 tokens (queries past 1024,
  documents past it to 4096): the engine-side and counting-side ids must be
  identical (R29).
- The probe-image check (one image, usage.prompt_tokens <= 1 + 2 + 1758);
  the served image path runs the checkpoint's own chat template through
  AutoProcessor.
- Never send an image query (media_sides); assert the negative case (the
  client's typed refusal). An image document's reply carries the render's
  kept vectors (the rule drops no media position; the head and vision markers
  stay), the client's declared count is checked against it, and the row
  carries no skip_unapplied: verify their geometry and tokens, and score them
  against the reference only with that rule declared.
- The compile risk above: watch for the context-9b crash; --enforce-eager is
  the declared fallback.
- The plugin wheel loads (T0), and the wave's pip freeze before/after differs
  by exactly that wheel; `import fla` must FAIL inside the engine image (the
  fla canary: the engine parsed config.json through vLLM's native qwen3_5
  config and never executed remote code -- this checkpoint carries none).

Record hygiene: the TEXT prompt paths ("[Q] " / "[D] " by name) are asserted
by this recipe's template data and its stage-1 render check; the image
